implemented: Shell API v16 exposes separate final Cloud approval and read-only execution recovery for the same saved delegation ID.
The native screen presents a final confirmation with the exact Wallet cap and explicit notice that the Cloud task can continue while the device is offline.
Approval requires the existing exact quote-bound HELD reservation, active same-device broker proof, and owner-authenticated Cloud state readback before sending the explicit PATCH approval.
The Broker never automatically repeats an approval request. If its result may be unknown, it fences the local Wallet cap as INDETERMINATE and requires a same-ID readback.
Cloud readback can reconcile a still-HELD local reservation after an app restart when it proves approval was accepted; settlement sync performs this before requiring a dispatched reservation.

The Wallet cap can be released only after Cloud readback proves the task remains awaiting approval with expired proof, or ended before dispatch; accepted, active, or unknown Cloud states cannot be released.
The production Cloud A2A execution feature flag remains disabled by default; this implementation does not enable paid dispatch.
Android task detail now shows verified A2A progress events and bounded provider-signed usage lines for provisional live snapshots and the final receipt; mismatched line totals are suppressed.

Android direct-LLM task detail now shows final rate-card token categories and charges. During execution it truthfully labels provider current usage as not reported and displays the reserved maximum separately.

The foreground Cloud home polls active tasks only while visible, at a server-requested bounded interval (10–120 seconds); polling stops when the screen pauses and the existing validated-connectivity callback refreshes after reconnect.
The final Cloud confirmation displays both the Agent-task cap and the parent-job cap so parallel child work stays within the user-approved envelope.
